//: TASK-S2-O4 (2026-09-24). The Node built-ins whose availability window starts ABOVE this repository's declared floor, as DATA rather than as a literal table inside runtime-floor.ts. That is not a style choice: the scanner matches literal substrings, so a table written in the validator's own source makes the validator its own worst offender -- the first run reported 15 violations, every one of them a row of its own table. `adr-status.ts` hit the identical trap one task earlier and solved it with per-line markers; a JSON file the scanner does not read is the cheaper half of the same fix, and it is the shape min-peer-lane.json and vue-next-lane.json already use.
//curation: Deliberately SHORT. A row earns its place by three tests: (1) the availability window starts above 20.19.0; (2) it is reached by importing or calling a name that can be matched textually, with no type checker; (3) its absence is a hard `TypeError` or `ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE`, not a quiet behaviour change. This is a floor on the floor -- it catches the class of break that has actually happened in this repository twice. It is NOT a complete Node compatibility analysis and must not be read as one.
//excluded-on-purpose: `Set.prototype.union`, `.intersection` and `.difference` are all @since v22.0.0 and all three are omitted, because `.union(`, `.intersection(` and `.difference(` are ordinary method names in ordinary user code and a gate with a false positive earns an allowlist entry and then gets switched off. The four Set methods below are kept because no plausible user-defined method is called `symmetricDifference`, `isSubsetOf`, `isSupersetOf` or `isDisjointFrom`.
//kinds: `module` = an import of the built-in module itself. `named-import` = the name must appear in the same statement as the module specifier. `member` = a literal property-access substring, matched anywhere.
